# enumeration-drift-fixtures.txt — labelled expected-verdict set for the enumeration-drift check
#
# PROVENANCE. These cases are the labelled fixture set of the enumeration <-> population
# drift check (core/deploy/tools/check-enumeration-drift.py, deploy.sh Check 83), written
# with the check by its introducing release. Case 1 is the seeded mismatch the check must
# flag, and case 2 its near-miss — the same document as a true `subset-of` — which it must
# not flag; together they are the control arm the check's acceptance criteria require.
# The remaining cases pin each binding, key and relation rule the tool's module docstring
# states, one rule per case, so a regression names the rule it broke.
#
# FORMAT (case-block, because a marked enumeration is irreducibly multi-line):
#   --- <EXPECT> <RELATION> <label>
#   POPULATION: <repo-relative path> ...      (required; may be empty)
#   DOCUMENT: <repo-relative path>            (optional; default fixture.md; sets the
#                                              directory a relative link resolves from)
#   <document lines>
#   --- END
# where
#   <EXPECT> = DRIFT       at least 1 DRIFT row and 0 UNRESOLVED rows
#            | CLEAN       at least 1 marker examined and 0 rows
#            | UNRESOLVED  at least 1 UNRESOLVED row and 0 DRIFT rows
#            | SCOPE-OUT   0 markers examined
#   <RELATION> = count | list | subset-of — the relation the case exercises (a label; a
#                malformed case cannot carry a parseable relation in its marker)
# POPULATION stands in for the tracked-file list, so a case runs with no git and no
# filesystem; the glob is matched against it exactly as against `git ls-files`.
#
# WHY EACH ARM IS LOAD-BEARING — read before tuning the tool against it.
# A CLEAN case that examines zero markers is a FAILURE, not a pass: "not flagged" and
# "not examined" are different verdicts, which is why SCOPE-OUT exists as its own
# expectation (the Check 63 fixture set's rule, reused). A DRIFT case that comes back
# UNRESOLVED is a FAILURE too: an unreadable marker is a finding, but it is not the drift
# the case seeds, and a tool that cannot bind the seeded list would pass a looser test.
#   - Cases 1 and 2 are the same items: only the relation differs. A tool that flags both
#     cannot tell `subset-of` from `list`; a tool that flags neither cannot see drift.
#   - Cases 3 to 6 pin each relation in both directions: an exact list, an extra member
#     under `subset-of`, an understated count, and a number word that reconciles.
#   - Case 7 pins segment-equal matching: a `*` that crossed `/` would make the nested
#     file a member and case 7 would drift.
#   - Cases 8 and 9 bound the preamble allowance at exactly one prose line.
#   - Cases 10 to 13 each seed one UNRESOLVED reason, so a marker the tool cannot read is
#     reported, never skipped as clean.
#   - Case 14 pins the fence rule: a marker quoted inside a fence is not a marker.
#   - Cases 15 and 16 pin wildcard-segment keys: every member is named SKILL.md, so a
#     basename key could neither key the list nor stay silent on the count.
#   - Cases 17 and 18 pin link resolution from the document's own directory, a leading
#     `/` from the root, and an off-glob link reading as extra rather than vanishing.
#   - Case 19 pins the code-span key of a glob with two wildcard segments.
#   - Case 20 pins the `dup` rule: every member is listed once and one is listed again,
#     so `missing` and `extra` are empty and only the repeat can drift. Case 3 is its
#     near-miss: the same list without the repeat.
# Cases: 6 DRIFT · 8 CLEAN · 5 UNRESOLVED · 1 SCOPE-OUT — 20 in all.

--- DRIFT list seeded-mismatch
POPULATION: pop/alpha.sh pop/beta.sh pop/gamma.sh
<!-- enumerates: pop/*.sh list -->

--- END
